newsitem.title: USA: Cyprus '97 capital spending put at $400 mln.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus '97 capital spending put at $400 mln.

text.p: Cyprus Amax Minerals said its capital expenditure in 1997 will total about $400 million, with a similar amount earmarked for 1998.

Of the $400 million total, $70 million will be spent on bringing its Amax Gold subsidiary's wholly-owned Fort Knox gold mine on stream in the current quarter, and starting up Amax Gold's partly owned Kubaka gold project in Russia, Cyprus chairman, president and CEO Milton Ward told an analyst briefing Wednesday.
A further $150 million will be spent on capital maintenance in the copper division, and $120 million on coal operations. The balance of the $400 million will be spent on capital maintenance.
Next year's capital expenditure will be used to raise output at the Cerro Verde copper mine in Peru and on further developments in Cyprus' coal operations.

Significant hikes in low-cost copper production and new gold projects coming on stream "will enable us to generate some meaningful cash flow beginning in 1997 and to use this to reduce our debt levels," Ward said.
